result:
Decision is **CONTINUE**: round 368 redoes the round-367 task (PERF-9b-ii, stem-cache hardening) with a fix for the bug that failed it. I touched only planning files; the store tree still holds A's uncommitted round-367 work, unchanged by me.

**Round 367 result (from C's report).**
- The round FAILED, so the root gate skipped it and the baseline is still `d53d113`.
- A stopped on a Medium that the code reviewer found and I had not ruled on; C reproduced it. When a demo sound's first load is cancelled and the same sound is loaded again, neither load caches it, so it downloads again next time. It costs speed only, with no wrong bytes and no data loss.
- C's browser checks all passed on round 367's code, at both screen sizes:
  - recovery from a truncated or deleted cached file;
  - a stale cache tag being replaced;
  - playback, and the WAV export;
  - anonymous `/studio-lab`, and purchase protection.
- PERF-9b-ii is still not done, and nothing moved to მზადაა.

**My ruling on the Medium.** When the same sound is loaded again while its first save is still waiting, the second load now joins that save instead of being dropped. The save is cancelled only if every load that joined it was cancelled. This caches the sound in every case the published code did. The one case it still misses is a cancel while the file is still downloading, and the published code misses that too. I rejected A's other two options; the reasons are in `b-round-367/sketch-review.md`.

**Round 368 task** (`current-task.md`; round 367's task copied to `tasks/round-367.md`):
- **Code:** the same 3 files. A applies `b-round-367/sketch-delta.patch.txt` on top of the current tree.
- **Tests:**
  - SC30 and SC31 cover the join.
  - SC32 covers a delete arriving while a save of the same sound is still downloading. C's round-367 mutant showed this had no test, and it is not harmless.
  - SC33 covers a cancel during the full-storage retry.
  - SC22's title is narrowed so it no longer claims more than it tests.
- **Doc 236:** the status line becomes `Completed (C round 368 PASS)`, and the doc stops claiming tests that do not exist.
- **C's checks:** C reruns its own round-367 cache probe on the new code, plus all the browser checks at both sizes and the purchase-protection check.

**My checks on the sketch, run on a scratch copy:**
- Round 367's code fails only SC30 and SC31 of the new tests, so those two tests catch the bug.
- C's own cache probe now stores the sound in both scenarios.
- All 19 deliberately broken versions of the code fail their intended tests.
- The full test suite passes (250 files, 3688 tests), and typecheck and Biome are clean.
- A production build at 1440×900 and 1280×720 behaves the same as in C's round-367 run.
- tech-lead reviewed this exact final version and found nothing Medium or higher. I fixed its two test gaps; this time the version reviewed is the one sent to A, which was the gap behind round 367.

**Backlog and board.** The bug-tracking and planning files are updated: backlog v331, decisions D-29z1206 to D-29z1209, and `feature-status.md`.
- C's three findings and the reviewer's doc-related Lows are targeted at round 368.
- Five other Lows go to `deferred_low_polish`.
- The reviewer's architecture note is recorded as a signal for the existing checkpoint request with root, not as a task.
- The retrospective moves to round 369, because the unpublished round-367 work has to be fixed first.
- The regression round is due on or after 2026-11-08.

The advisor was available and I used it before the ruling and for the final check. For tech-lead and the advisor I record only the conclusions, in `sketch-review.md` and `b-round-367.md`.

Everything is in `tmp/studio-real-loop/`: `current-task.md`, `b-round-367.md`, `b-next.json`, and the evidence under `b-round-367/`.
